stem.en:
The ferry to Kestrel Island leaves the harbour at 7.40 every morning and reaches the island jetty 55 minutes later. The island itself is only 4 kilometres long, so most visitors explore it on foot or hire a bicycle at the jetty. On Sundays the first boat leaves later, at 9.15, and the last boat back leaves the island at 6 in the evening.

How much time does the boat trip to the island take?

why.en: "55 minutes": the ferry reaches the island "55 minutes later". "4 kilometres long" shares the word "long", but it is the size of the island.
why.uz: «55 minutes»: parom orolga «55 minutes later» yetadi. «4 kilometres long» — orolning uzunligi, safar vaqti emas.
why.ru: «55 minutes»: паром прибывает «55 minutes later». «4 kilometres long» — это длина острова, а не время в пути.

stem.en:
The Fairfield Youth Theatre was started twelve years ago by two drama teachers who wanted to give local teenagers a stage of their own. It now has 85 members aged 11 to 18, and together they stage three plays a year. Each play is performed twice, on a Friday and a Saturday evening, in the hall of the old library.

How many productions does the group put on every year?

why.en: "three": the members "stage three plays a year". "Twice" is how often each play is performed, and "two" is the number of teachers.
why.uz: «three»: aʼzolar yiliga «three plays» sahnalashtiradi. «Twice» — har bir spektakl necha marta koʻrsatilishi, «two» — oʻqituvchilar soni.
why.ru: «three»: участники ставят «three plays a year». «Twice» — сколько раз идёт каждый спектакль, «two» — число учителей.

stem.en:
Tickets for the Hilltop music weekend go on sale on the first of May. Last year all 4,000 tickets were sold within six days, and many fans were disappointed. This year the organisers have added a second stage and opened a new field for tents, so the festival will have room for 5,500 people over the two days. Camping tickets are sold separately.

How many people will be able to attend the festival this year?

why.en: "5,500": this year the festival "will have room for 5,500 people". 4,000 was last year's number of tickets.
why.uz: «5,500»: bu yil festivalda «room for 5,500 people» boʻladi. 4,000 — oʻtgan yilgi chiptalar soni.
why.ru: «5,500»: в этом году на фестивале «room for 5,500 people». 4,000 — число билетов в прошлом году.

stem.en:
Mrs Okafor's cookery class meets in the kitchen of Lindale Community Centre every Thursday. Each class lasts two hours and costs eight pounds, which includes all the ingredients and the use of aprons. Learners take home whatever they cook, so they are asked to bring a plastic box with a lid. No cooking experience is needed, and beginners are always welcome.

What container should learners come with?

options.en: a plastic box with a lid

why.en: "a plastic box with a lid": learners "are asked to bring" one. The ingredients and the aprons are included in the price.
why.uz: «a plastic box with a lid»: oʻquvchilardan uni «bring» qilish soʻraladi. Masalliqlar va fartuklar narxga kiritilgan.
why.ru: «a plastic box with a lid»: учеников просят «bring» его. Продукты и фартуки уже входят в цену.

stem.en:
The Westmarsh bird count takes place on the last weekend of every January. Volunteers spend one hour at a spot of their choice and write down every bird they see. In the first count, in 2015, 120 volunteers took part. Last winter 640 people joined in, and between them they recorded 52 different kinds of bird. The results are put on the town website in March.

How many people helped in the most recent count?

why.en: "640": "Last winter 640 people joined in". The word "volunteers" sits next to 120, but that was the first count, in 2015.
why.uz: «640»: «Last winter 640 people joined in». «volunteers» soʻzi 120 yonida turibdi, lekin bu 2015-yildagi birinchi sanoq.
why.ru: «640»: «Last winter 640 people joined in». Слово «volunteers» стоит рядом со 120, но это первый подсчёт, 2015 год.

stem.en:
The new footbridge over the River Lenn took eighteen months to build and cost far more than planned. It is 90 metres long and wide enough for two wheelchairs to pass each other. Before it opened, people living on the east bank had to make a 3-kilometre detour through the town to reach the railway station. At night the bridge is lit by small lamps set into its rails.

How far out of their way did east-bank residents have to go before the bridge opened?

why.en: "3 kilometres": they "had to make a 3-kilometre detour". A detour is going out of your way; 90 metres is the length of the bridge.
why.uz: «3 kilometres»: ular «3-kilometre detour» qilishga majbur edi. Detour — aylanma yoʻl; 90 metr — koʻprik uzunligi.
why.ru: «3 kilometres»: им приходилось делать «3-kilometre detour», то есть крюк. 90 метров — длина моста.

stem.en:
At the Sandal Cross recycling centre, glass, paper and metal are collected every day, but garden waste is accepted only at weekends between April and October. Large items such as sofas and beds can be collected from homes for a fee of fifteen pounds, which must be paid when the collection is booked. Batteries and old paint must be taken to the main depot in town.

When do you pay to have a sofa taken away?

options.en: on the day the sofa is collected

why.en: "when the collection is booked": the fee "must be paid when the collection is booked", not on the day the sofa is taken.
why.uz: «when the collection is booked»: toʻlov «must be paid when the collection is booked», divan olib ketiladigan kuni emas.
why.ru: «when the collection is booked»: плата «must be paid when the collection is booked», а не в день вывоза дивана.

stem.en:
Founded by a group of retired teachers, the Greystone reading club began with six members who met in a kitchen. Within two years it had outgrown the kitchen and moved to the town library. Today about forty readers meet there on the first Wednesday of each month, and a second group, for teenagers, meets on the third Saturday. New members are always welcome.

How often does the original group meet now?

why.en: "once a month": the readers meet "on the first Wednesday of each month". The third Saturday is the teenagers' group.
why.uz: «once a month»: ular «on the first Wednesday of each month» yigʻiladi. Uchinchi shanba — oʻsmirlar guruhi.
why.ru: «once a month»: они встречаются «on the first Wednesday of each month». Третья суббота — у группы подростков.

stem.en:
Only one doctor serves the island, and she visits from the mainland to hold a surgery every Tuesday. In an emergency, patients are flown to Port Ellery by helicopter, a journey of 25 minutes. If the weather is too bad to fly, they are taken by lifeboat instead, which takes nearly two hours in a calm sea. Medicines can be collected from the island shop.

If bad weather stops flights, how long does it take to get a patient to Port Ellery?

why.en: "nearly two hours": when it is "too bad to fly", the lifeboat goes, and it "takes nearly two hours". 25 minutes is the helicopter.
why.uz: «nearly two hours»: havo «too bad to fly» boʻlsa, qutqaruv qayigʻi boradi va «takes nearly two hours». 25 daqiqa — vertolyot.
why.ru: «nearly two hours»: когда погода «too bad to fly», идёт спасательная лодка — «nearly two hours». 25 минут — вертолёт.

stem.en:
Entry to the Corran Valley Museum is free for under-16s and for anyone on their birthday. Adults pay seven pounds, and students with a valid card pay half that price. On the last Friday of each month the museum stays open until 9 p.m., and from 5 p.m. on those evenings adults get in for four pounds. Guided tours are included in the price.

On an ordinary afternoon, how much does an adult with a valid student card pay?

why.en: "£3.50": adults pay seven pounds and students with a card "pay half that price". £4 is only for late Friday evenings.
why.uz: «£3.50»: kattalar yetti funt toʻlaydi, karta bilan talabalar esa «half that price». £4 — faqat juma oqshomlarida.
why.ru: «£3.50»: взрослые платят семь фунтов, студенты с картой — «half that price». £4 — только поздним вечером пятницы.

stem.en:
When Greenhill School asked pupils to leave their phones in lockers at lunchtime, many people expected complaints. Instead, the playground grew louder. Pupils started playing old games again, the chess club doubled in size, and teachers noticed fewer arguments in afternoon lessons. After one term, the pupils' own council voted to keep the rule for the rest of the year.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A rule that worked better than expected
The chess club doubles in size after one term
Pupils protest against a new rule

why.en: "A rule that worked better than expected": people feared complaints, but every result is good. Chess and arguments are details.
why.uz: «A rule that worked better than expected»: shikoyat kutilgan edi, lekin barcha natijalar yaxshi. Shaxmat va tortishuvlar — tafsilotlar.
why.ru: «A rule that worked better than expected»: ждали жалоб, но все итоги хорошие. Шахматы и споры — детали.

stem.en:
Until last year, the last bus from Holt Bridge to the city centre left at nine in the evening. Nurses, cleaners and kitchen staff who finished work late had to pay for taxis or walk home for an hour. In January a night bus was introduced, running every forty minutes until two in the morning. In its first month it carried more passengers than the morning service.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A new service for people who work late
Problems with the early morning bus service
Walking to work to stay healthy

why.en: "A new service for people who work late": the paragraph goes from the problem (no late bus) to the night bus. Taxis are one detail of the problem.
why.uz: «A new service for people who work late»: xatboshi muammodan (kechki avtobus yoʻq) tungi avtobusga oʻtadi. Taksi — muammoning bir tafsiloti.
why.ru: «A new service for people who work late»: абзац ведёт от проблемы (нет позднего автобуса) к ночному рейсу. Такси — деталь.

stem.en:
Lost something on a train in Dalwick? Until recently, you had to phone each station and hope that someone had written it down. Now every item found on the trains is photographed and put on a website within a day. Owners can search by date and by line, and most bags, umbrellas and phones are back with their owners in less than a week.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A faster way to get lost things back
Why so many people forget their umbrellas on trains

why.en: "A faster way to get lost things back": the old slow way, then a website that returns items within a week. Phones and lines are details.
why.uz: «A faster way to get lost things back»: eski sekin usul, keyin narsalarni bir haftada qaytaradigan sayt. Telefonlar va liniyalar — tafsilot.
why.ru: «A faster way to get lost things back»: старый медленный способ, затем сайт, который возвращает вещи за неделю. Телефоны — деталь.

stem.en:
Every Tuesday evening, the back room of the Copper Kettle café turns into a language class without a teacher. Tables are marked with small flags, and people sit where they want to practise: Spanish, Korean, Turkish or English. Someone who speaks a language well helps a learner for half an hour, and then they swap. Nobody pays, but everyone is asked to buy a drink.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Learning languages by helping each other
The café's new menu of drinks
How to train as a language teacher

why.en: "Learning languages by helping each other": people practise in pairs and swap roles. The flags and the drinks are small details.
why.uz: «Learning languages by helping each other»: odamlar juft boʻlib mashq qiladi va rollarni almashadi. Bayroqchalar va ichimliklar — mayda tafsilotlar.
why.ru: «Learning languages by helping each other»: люди занимаются в парах и меняются ролями. Флажки и напитки — мелкие детали.

stem.en:
The hut below Grey Peak is open all year, but in winter nobody is there to run it. Walkers who stay must bring their own food and fuel, and they are asked to leave the hut as clean as they found it. A book by the door records who stayed and when they plan to reach the valley, so that rescuers know where to look if someone goes missing.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Rules for staying in the winter hut
Why the hut closes in winter
The best routes up Grey Peak
How rescuers search for walkers who go missing

why.en: "Rules for staying in the winter hut": bring food and fuel, clean up, sign the book. The hut is open all year, and rescuers are one detail.
why.uz: «Rules for staying in the winter hut»: ovqat va yoqilgʻi olib keling, tozalang, daftarga yozing. Kulba yil boʻyi ochiq; qutqaruvchilar — tafsilot.
why.ru: «Rules for staying in the winter hut»: возьмите еду и топливо, уберите, запишитесь в книгу. Хижина открыта весь год; спасатели — деталь.

stem.en:
Two years ago, the space behind Ashby Lane Primary School was a car park. Today it is a garden where every class grows one vegetable. The youngest children grow beans, because they come up quickly; older pupils try harder crops such as peppers. Everything they pick is cooked in the school kitchen, and children who once refused vegetables now ask for more.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A school that grows its own vegetables
Children who once refused to eat any vegetables

why.en: "A school that grows its own vegetables": the garden, the crops and the school kitchen. The beans and the old car park are details.
why.uz: «A school that grows its own vegetables»: bogʻ, ekinlar va maktab oshxonasi. Loviya va eski avtoturargoh — tafsilotlar.
why.ru: «A school that grows its own vegetables»: огород, урожай и школьная кухня. Фасоль и бывшая парковка — детали.

stem.en:
Radio Linden is run entirely by teenagers. Every Saturday, a team of twelve students aged 14 to 17 plans, records and presents a two-hour programme. They interview local shopkeepers, read out the football results and play music chosen by listeners. Adults look after the equipment, but the students decide everything that goes on air. Most of them had never spoken into a microphone before they joined.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

Buying new equipment for a local radio station

why.en: "A radio programme made by young people": the teenagers plan, record and present it. Football and music are only parts of the show.
why.uz: «A radio programme made by young people»: oʻsmirlar uni rejalashtiradi, yozadi va olib boradi. Futbol va musiqa — koʻrsatuvning bir qismi.
why.ru: «A radio programme made by young people»: подростки сами планируют, записывают и ведут её. Футбол и музыка — лишь части передачи.

stem.en:
A  The village of Steeple Moss stands on a hill above a wide river. For two hundred years its people farmed the valley below and crossed the water by a narrow wooden bridge.

B  When a winter flood swept the bridge away, the village was cut off for three months. Children could not reach their school and farmers could not sell their milk. The disaster finally persuaded the regional government to build a stone bridge, which still stands, and the village began to grow again.

Choose the best heading for paragraph B.

options.en: A loss that led to a lasting change
A village on a hill above a wide river
How the first bridge was built

why.en: "A loss that led to a lasting change": B goes from the lost bridge to the new stone one. The hill and the river describe A; the milk is a detail.
why.uz: «A loss that led to a lasting change»: B yoʻqolgan koʻprikdan yangi tosh koʻprikka oʻtadi. Tepalik va daryo — A haqida; sut — tafsilot.
why.ru: «A loss that led to a lasting change»: B ведёт от смытого моста к новому каменному. Холм и река — это A; молоко — деталь.

stem.en:
Some visitors complain that the Hartwell Museum is too quiet. There are no screens, no buttons to press and no music in the halls. Each room holds only a few objects, with short labels and plenty of chairs. This is deliberate: the founder wanted a place where people look slowly at one thing at a time instead of hurrying past hundreds.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: A museum built for slow looking

why.en: "A museum built for slow looking": the last sentence explains every choice before it. Visitors find it too quiet, not too noisy.
why.uz: «A museum built for slow looking»: oxirgi gap oldingi barcha tanlovlarni tushuntiradi. Tashrif buyuruvchilar shovqindan emas, jimlikdan shikoyat qiladi.
why.ru: «A museum built for slow looking»: последнее предложение объясняет всё, что перед ним. Посетители жалуются на тишину, а не на шум.

stem.en:
Pupils at Brookside Academy have read a small weather station on the school roof twice a day for six years. Their records of rain and temperature were meant only for science lessons. But last autumn, when the river rose, local farmers began asking the school for its rainfall figures, because the nearest official station is forty kilometres away. The pupils now put their readings online every evening.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: School weather data that farmers use
Science lessons on the school roof
How official weather stations collect data

why.en: "School weather data that farmers use": the records were for lessons, then farmers needed them. The text never says farms were ruined.
why.uz: «School weather data that farmers use»: yozuvlar dars uchun edi, keyin fermerlarga kerak boʻldi. Fermalar vayron boʻlgani aytilmagan.
why.ru: «School weather data that farmers use»: записи вели для уроков, потом они понадобились фермерам. О разорённых фермах ни слова.

stem.en:
At first, Dilnoza sold only one dish from her food cart: plov, cooked in a huge pan at the corner of the station square. Office workers loved it, but by two o'clock the pan was empty and the cart stood idle for the rest of the day. So she added evening dishes: soup in winter and cold noodles in summer. Within a year her takings had doubled, and she now employs two of her cousins.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Making a small business work all day
How to cook plov in a huge pan for a crowd

why.en: "Making a small business work all day": the cart stood idle after lunch, so she added evening dishes and earned more. Plov and cousins are details.
why.uz: «Making a small business work all day»: tushdan keyin arava boʻsh turardi, u kechki taomlar qoʻshib, koʻproq ishladi. Palov va qarindoshlar — tafsilot.
why.ru: «Making a small business work all day»: после обеда тележка простаивала, она добавила вечерние блюда и стала зарабатывать больше.

stem.en:
In the new district of Fernway, planners placed the shops, the school and the health centre within ten minutes' walk of every home. Streets were made narrow to slow down cars, and wide paths were laid for bicycles. Five years on, most residents say they rarely use their cars on weekdays, and the district's two car parks are often half empty.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Empty car parks in the city centre
The cost of building narrow streets

why.en: "A district built for walking": the plan and its result both point there. The half-empty car parks are in Fernway, not the city centre.
why.uz: «A district built for walking»: reja ham, natija ham shunga ishora qiladi. Yarim boʻsh avtoturargohlar shahar markazida emas, Fernwayda.
why.ru: «A district built for walking»: и замысел, и итог ведут к этому. Полупустые парковки — в Fernway, а не в центре.

instructions.ru: Выберите наиболее подходящий заголовок для абзаца.

stem.en:
Paper maps were once kept in every car. Today most drivers follow their phones, and petrol stations no longer sell road atlases. Yet in the hills around Hobb Fell, the mountain rescue team still hands out free paper maps at every car park. Phone signals there are weak, batteries run down quickly in the cold, and the team says a paper map has helped more lost walkers than any app.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Why paper maps still matter in the hills
The end of the road atlas
Keeping phone batteries warm on cold mountains

why.en: "Why paper maps still matter in the hills": the first two sentences only set the scene. "The end of the road atlas" fits them, not the paragraph.

Most households own a drill that is used for only a few minutes a year. In Wexley, residents found a better way: a library of tools in an empty shop on the high street. Members pay a small yearly fee and can borrow ladders, drills, sewing machines and even a carpet cleaner for up to a week. The scheme saves money, and it means fewer machines sit unused in cupboards.

Empty shops on the high street
How to use a drill safely

stem.en:
For most of its history, Port Hallam's fish market sold whatever the boats brought in, and prices rose and fell with each catch. Then a few crews began taking orders by phone from restaurants the evening before they sailed. Knowing what was wanted, they caught less, wasted less and agreed their prices in advance. Other boats soon joined them, and the market's early-morning auction is now a fraction of its former size.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Fishing to order changes the market
How each catch affects fish prices
The decline of the local fishing industry
Restaurants that buy only fresh fish

why.en: "Fishing to order changes the market": crews sell before they sail, and the auction shrinks. The auction is smaller, but fishing is not said to decline.
why.uz: «Fishing to order changes the market»: baliqchilar dengizga chiqishdan oldin sotadi, auksion kichrayadi. Baliqchilik pasaygani aytilmagan.
why.ru: «Fishing to order changes the market»: рыбаки продают улов заранее, и аукцион сжимается. Об упадке самого промысла не сказано.

stem.en:
Visitors to the Saltmarsh Reserve once walked wherever they liked. Over the years their footsteps wore wide bare tracks across the marsh, and ground-nesting birds abandoned the busiest areas. Rather than closing the reserve, the managers built a single raised boardwalk and asked people to keep to it. Within three seasons, plants had covered the old tracks and the birds were nesting close to the boardwalk itself.

Choose the best heading for this paragraph.

options.en: Saving wildlife without closing the reserve
Why the reserve was closed to the public
The harm done by careless walkers over the years
Rare plants of the salt marsh

why.en: "Saving wildlife without closing the reserve": the harm is only the first half; the boardwalk fixes it while people still come. It never closed.
why.uz: «Saving wildlife without closing the reserve»: zarar — faqat birinchi yarmi; yoʻlak uni tuzatadi, odamlar kelaveradi. Qoʻriqxona yopilmagan.
why.ru: «Saving wildlife without closing the reserve»: вред — лишь первая половина; настил решает проблему, люди приходят. Заповедник не закрывали.

Instead of a bigger main pool, people asked for a shallow pool for learners, longer opening hours and changing rooms for families. The new building has all three, and the weekend queues have gone.

The end of the weekend queues

why.ru: «Asking residents before building»: B — о том, что просили жители и что получили. Старый бассейн — мысль A, очереди — последняя деталь B.

When the Rowan Hill hospital opened a garden on its roof, the aim was to give patients a pleasant place to sit. Staff, however, soon became its most frequent visitors. stem.en:
A ticket to the Fenmoor Arts Festival costs less than a cinema seat. The organisers keep the price low by relying on volunteers, borrowing chairs from local schools and holding most events in the open air. The result is more than a cheap weekend: half of last year's audience said it was their first time at a live performance of any kind.

The volunteers who run the festival
Why cinema seats cost so much

why.ru: «Low prices that bring in new audiences»: как держат низкую цену и кого она приводит. Волонтёры — один из способов, деталь.

From empty mill to busy centre
Why the textile mill stopped making cloth
Artists move into an old mill

The Hollis family keep their cheeses in a tunnel because its steady, cool temperature is ideal while the cheeses ______. This has cut their electricity bills.

why.en: "ripen": the temperature "is exactly what their cheeses need while they ripen". "mature" means the same, but it is not a word from the text.
why.uz: «ripen»: harorat «is exactly what their cheeses need while they ripen». «mature» maʼnosi bir xil, lekin u matndagi soʻz emas.
why.ru: «ripen»: температура «is exactly what their cheeses need while they ripen». «mature» значит то же, но этого слова в тексте нет.

stem.en:
The village hall at Brenley was built almost a century ago and badly needed repairs. Instead of asking the council for money, residents held a year of events: a quiz night every month, a summer fair and a sponsored walk along the old canal towpath. Together these raised enough to mend the leaking roof, and the walk alone paid for new heating.

Complete the sentence. Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text.

The money for the hall's new heating came from the ______.

why.en: "sponsored walk": "the walk alone paid for new heating", and that walk is the sponsored one. All the events together paid for the roof.
why.uz: «sponsored walk»: «the walk alone paid for new heating», bu yurish esa homiylik yurishi. Barcha tadbirlar birgalikda tomni taʼmirlagan.
why.ru: «sponsored walk»: «the walk alone paid for new heating», а эта прогулка и есть спонсорская. Все события вместе оплатили крышу.

stem.en:
Most visitors to the island of Skerrin come for its seabirds, which nest on the western cliffs from May to July. Fewer people know about the island's eastern shore, where a sheltered bay is home to a colony of grey seals. The seals are easiest to see in autumn, and at that time the island's boatman runs special trips round to the bay.

Complete the summary. Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text.

Skerrin is best known for the birds on its western cliffs, but in autumn the boatman also takes visitors to see ______ in a bay on the east of the island.

why.en: "grey seals": the bay on the eastern shore "is home to a colony of grey seals", and the autumn trips go there. The seabirds are on the west.
why.uz: «grey seals»: sharqiy qirgʻoqdagi koʻrfaz «is home to a colony of grey seals», kuzgi sayohatlar oʻsha yerga. Dengiz qushlari — gʻarbda.
why.ru: «grey seals»: бухта на восточном берегу «is home to a colony of grey seals», туда и идут осенние рейсы. Морские птицы — на западе.

stem.en:
At the Tamsin Road community kitchen, volunteers cook a free hot meal every Sunday for anyone who wants one. Local supermarkets give food that is close to its sell-by date, and a nearby farm sends whatever vegetables it cannot sell. The volunteers plan the menu on Saturday evening, once they know what has arrived, so no two Sunday meals are ever the same.

Complete the sentence. Use ONE WORD ONLY from the text.

The Sunday menu changes every week because it depends on the food that has ______.

why.en: "arrived": volunteers plan the menu "once they know what has arrived". "delivered" means much the same, but it is not the word in the text.
why.uz: «arrived»: koʻngillilar menyuni «once they know what has arrived» tuzadi. «delivered» maʼnosi yaqin, lekin matndagi soʻz emas.
why.ru: «arrived»: меню составляют «once they know what has arrived». «delivered» значит почти то же, но в тексте другое слово.

stem.en:
The town of Halsey Cross holds its winter lights festival on the longest night of the year. For one evening, every street light is switched off, and the streets are lit instead by thousands of candles in glass jars made by local schoolchildren. The festival began as a way to save energy, but it is now the town's busiest night, with visitors arriving on special trains.

Complete the summary. Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text.

On one winter night, Halsey Cross turns off its street lights and uses candles in ______ made by children.

why.en: "glass jars": the streets are lit "by thousands of candles in glass jars made by local schoolchildren". "paper lanterns" is not in the text.
why.uz: «glass jars»: koʻchalar «by thousands of candles in glass jars made by local schoolchildren» yoritiladi. «paper lanterns» matnda yoʻq.
why.ru: «glass jars»: улицы освещают «thousands of candles in glass jars made by local schoolchildren». «paper lanterns» в тексте нет.

stem.en:
The bus company in Orton Vale has replaced the paper timetables at its stops with small solar-powered screens. Each screen shows when the next three buses will arrive, using signals sent from the buses themselves. Older passengers who found the screens hard to read asked for a change, so a button was added that reads the information aloud in a clear voice.

Complete the sentence. Use ONE WORD ONLY from the text.

The screens know when buses will arrive from ______ that the buses send.

why.en: "signals": the screens work "using signals sent from the buses themselves". "messages" is not in the text, and the paper timetables were removed.
why.uz: «signals»: ekranlar «using signals sent from the buses themselves» ishlaydi. «messages» matnda yoʻq, qogʻoz jadvallar esa olib tashlangan.
why.ru: «signals»: экраны работают «using signals sent from the buses themselves». «messages» в тексте нет, а бумажные расписания убрали.

stem.en:
Every August, the Mirren valley holds a sheepdog trial in which dogs must guide five sheep around a course and into a small pen. Each dog works alone with its handler, who may only whistle or call. Judges take away points whenever a sheep strays from the line, and the dog that loses the fewest points wins a silver crook, which its handler keeps for a year.

Complete the summary. Use NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the text.

Handlers guide their dogs only by whistling or calling. Points are lost when a sheep leaves the line, and the winner takes home a ______ for a year.

why.en: "silver crook": the winning dog "wins a silver crook", which its handler keeps for a year. "silver cup" is not in the text.
why.uz: «silver crook»: gʻolib it «wins a silver crook», uni egasi bir yil saqlaydi. «silver cup» matnda yoʻq.
why.ru: «silver crook»: победитель «wins a silver crook», и хозяин собаки хранит его год. «silver cup» в тексте нет.
